subject: Pre-sales: session transience & KV-cache impact questionnaire
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Liu <cara.liu@quantify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-sales: session transience & KV-cache impact questionnaire

Hi Cara / Quantify team,

Thanks for the demo last week — great conversation. Before we size Dedicated capacity for QNT-2026-0921 I wanted to capture a few specifics about your session lifecycle and how much value you expect to get from KV / prefix caching. I've attached our lightweight sizing template for your convenience (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx).

Short asks — if you can populate what you have and reply in-line that'd be ideal. If easier, a quick 30m call works too. Questions below:

1) Typical request pattern: do you use long-running sessions (conversational state kept across many turns) or mostly single-shot inference per user? If sessions, how many turns on average and distribution (p10/p50/p90)?

2) Prompt vs response token mix: approximate tokens for prompt, avg model completion tokens, and p95 completion length.

3) KV / prefix cache usage: do you rely on cached KV for most repeated prompts (e.g., system prompt + few-shot examples)? Estimate expected cache hit-rate during steady workload.

4) Concurrency and session stickiness: expected concurrent sessions vs concurrent active inference requests. Do you expect many idle sessions with attached KV caches?

5) Burst characteristics: peak requests per minute and duration of peak windows (minutes/hours). Any predictable daily cycles?

6) SLA targets & latency SLOs (p50/p95 generation latency targets). Are you using streaming?

7) Fault/fallback tolerance: do you want a model fallback to a smaller/quantized variant during overload?

8) Warmup & priming: are you able to warm a portion of the fleet ahead of scheduled peaks?

Attached: quantify_session_profile.csv — if you can drop a CSV of recent requests that maps token lengths and timestamps that will let us produce a more exact GPU footprint.

Thanks — looking forward to your data.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 64KB)
Attachment: quantify_session_profile.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Cara Liu <cara.liu@quantify.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@quantify.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: session transience & KV-cache impact questionnaire

Monica — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an initial pass (attached) and answered inline below; happy to refine. Short answers first: most traffic is conversational with sticky sessions, median turns ~= 6, p95 ~= 28; avg prompt tokens 180, avg completion 220, p95 completion 1,100 tokens; expected KV hit-rate ~65% during steady-state; we do use streaming for gameplay experiences.

Inline answers to your numbered list:
1) Session type: long-running sessions (retained across multiple app sessions). We keep conversation state server-side; average turns per user per session: p10=2, p50=6, p90=18, p95=28.

2) Token mix: prompt median 180, mean 210; completion median 220, mean 280; completion p95 1,100 (occasionally long generations for summarization).

3) KV/prefix caching: reuse system prompt + persona + 2-shot examples in ~70% of requests; after accounting for slightly different user inputs we estimate effective hit-rate 60–70% steady-state.

4) Concurrency & stickiness: peak concurrent active inference requests ~420 across all regions, but total concurrent sessions (idle + active) ~3,800. Session stickiness: we key sessions to instances for cache locality but expect 25% of active requests to miss local KV and require remote fetch.

5) Bursts: main daily peak is 11:30–13:30 PST with sustained 25–30 minute bursts; weekly campaign spikes (marketing) can produce 3–4hr elevated windows ~2x baseline. Peak requests per minute at the largest peak: ~1,100 RPM sustained for 20–30 minutes.

6) SLA / latency: target p50 generation <100ms, p95 <450ms for common prompts (short completions). For long completions (p95 1,100 tokens) our users accept higher tails up to 2.5s. We use streaming for UX; ideal is low first-byte latency.

7) Fallback: yes — we want an automatic fallback to a quantized variant under heavy load, but only for non-critical summarization jobs. Gameplay chat should not fallback.

8) Warmup: we can warm ~15% of expected peak capacity 10 minutes prior to scheduled campaigns; otherwise unscheduled peaks cannot be pre-warmed.

Attached: quantify_session_profile.csv (sample 48k rows) — note fields: timestamp, session_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, is_streaming, route_tag.

Hope this helps. Let us know if you need an export in a different shape.

—Cara
Cara Liu
Head of Product Operations | Quantify.ai
cara.liu@quantify.ai
Attachment: quantify_session_profile.csv (csv, 48KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Liu <cara.liu@quantify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: session transience & KV-cache impact questionnaire

Great, this is super helpful — thanks Cara. A couple follow-ups so our sizing can be concrete: 

- For the 60–70% effective KV hit-rate, can you estimate distribution by route_tag? If certain routes are near 90% hit-rate we can treat those as very cache-friendly and size accordingly.

- Can you confirm how often sessions become active after long idle windows (e.g., sessions that are restored after >12 hours)? That affects how much KV we must keep resident versus cold-restore cost.

- When you say 25% of active requests miss local KV and require remote fetch, is that symptomatic of cross-AZ routing or you intentionally shard sessions across instances?

Operationally: based on the data you provided I'm going to model two sizing scenarios and share a conservative and an optimistic footprint:

Conservative: assume 60% KV hit-rate, 25% remote KV misses, p95 completion 1,100 tokens, target p95 <450ms for short flows. Plan includes a 10% warm reserved buffer and 2X burst pool for marketing spikes.

Optimistic: assume 70% KV hit-rate, 10% remote KV misses, measured warmup of 15% successful — smaller fleet and fewer reserved GPUs.

Marissa / Karthik — can you weigh in on quantized fallback capacity assumptions (how much lower throughput for the quantized variant vs full fp16 for same GPU class)? Also, we should map burst pool to Dedicated autoscaling policy buckets. I'll attach the initial model once I run the sim.

Cara — can you send the per-route sample (route_tag) when you get a chance? Even a 30-row sample per route will let us bucketize.

Thanks — will follow up with the modeled footprint by EOD.

Best,
Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cara Liu <cara.liu@quantify.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-sales: session transience & KV-cache impact questionnaire

Monica / team — quick note from the sizing side:

- Quantized fallback throughput: for our commonly used A100-80GB class a 4-bit quantized variant gives ~1.8x throughput uplift at roughly 40% lower memory footprint vs fp16 for generation-heavy workloads. That implies a quantized fallback can absorb a ~35–45% load spike for non-streaming summarization jobs. Streaming sessions are more latency-sensitive and will see smaller effective gains (~1.3x) because of per-token overhead.

- Autoscaling buckets: recommend these buckets for Dedicated: baseline reserved pool (for steady-state) sized to optimistic scenario, warm buffer (15% nominal) pinned, burst pool (on-demand) sized to handle 2x baseline for short windows with cold start allowance ~60s.

- KV eviction plan: for large session counts (3,800 concurrent sessions with 25% cold misses) plan for a hybrid: keep hot prefix + persona caches resident; offload per-session long tail to fast remote store (redis/memcache). We should budget for extra network egress if remote fetches are common.

Monica — if you can drop the per-route sample into the Drive link Monica included I can run the sim tomorrow and populate the GPU SKU mix (A100-80GB vs H100 80GB vs M60 style high-density) and expected token-econ.

Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
